A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, renamed Local-Prompt in v2. Text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison. V1 ends with references; v2 adds Appendices A–E, which were included in the comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original few-shot OOD detection, ID classification, ablation, and visualization results.

after.justification: V2 retains the original experiments and adds comparator results, sensitivity experiments, and quantitative and visual analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Equation 7 changes the stated diversity objective from averaging all ordered prompt pairs, including self-pairs, to averaging distinct unordered pairs. This slightly changes its normalization. The architecture, augmentation procedure, other losses, and inference scores remain substantively unchanged; the PDFs do not establish an implementation change or rerunning of retained experiments.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-1k, ImageNet-100, and ImageNet-10/20, with iNaturalist, SUN, Places, and Texture for OOD evaluation. The additional shots, diagnostics, and illustrated cases remain within this coverage. Appendix A supplies subset details rather than introducing datasets.

E2.justification: V2 adds targeted comparisons with NegLabel in Table 5 and ID-like in Table 13. Its expanded density-map comparison also includes MCM alongside LoCoOp and the proposed method. The comparator sets in the retained main benchmark tables remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The supplementary evaluation design expands substantially: v2 adds an 8-shot condition, Gaussian-noise augmentation, loss-coefficient and training/testing regional-number sweeps, 30-versus-50-epoch comparisons, and one-versus-eight negative-crop comparisons. These are added experimental conditions. Newly disclosed defaults and validation-set details do not establish changes to the retained experiments.

E4.justification: V2 adds analyses of coefficient sensitivity, regional selection, longer training, and negative-augmentation count, plus a Gaussian-noise control. New hard-OOD examples, heatmaps, expanded density plots, and Table 14's local-similarity comparison examine detection mechanisms. The earlier score ablation remains as Figure 4, replacing its tabular presentation.

E5.justification: Appendix B newly states that reported results are averaged over three runs; v1 provides no run count. This is newly disclosed replication information, not evidence of an increase in runs. Neither version reports dispersion, confidence intervals, significance tests, or seed identities.

E6.justification: Main benchmark Tables 1–4 retain their values, but the L_pos+L_neg ablation changes from average FPR95/AUROC 28.59/93.42 in v1 Table 5 to 29.27/93.27 in v2 Table 6. V2 adds substantial comparator, 8-shot, sensitivity, and similarity results. Its proposed-method rows in Tables 5 and 13 reproduce Table 1's combined Local-Prompt+LoCoOp values despite abbreviated labels; they do not establish improved standalone performance between versions.

T1.justification: Equation 7 replaces the N_neg^2 normalization and all-pairs summation with normalization by N_neg(N_neg−1)/2 over i<j. This is a limited mathematical revision, not merely renamed notation. Other formal content remains equivalent or is clarified; no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: separate local prompts, negative augmentation, regional regularization and scoring, and compatibility with trained global prompts. The headline 5.17-point FPR95 reduction and claim that 4-shot results outperform earlier 16-shot methods remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendices C–E add substantive explanations of coefficient extremes, regional-selection tradeoffs, excess negative crops, and convergence. V2 also interprets hard-OOD cases and local-similarity separation, discusses NegLabel's external negative-label knowledge, and explicitly addresses training overhead, unexplored joint prompt training, and extension beyond classification.

D1.justification: V1 gives only limited implementation settings. V2 adds context length, SGD, learning rate and schedule, batch size, epochs, crop counts, training/testing k values, hardware, and training time. It also specifies dataset subsets and the validation set and adds a code-release link. These disclosures substantially improve reproducibility without establishing that the original settings changed.

R1.justification: V2 adds NegLabel, ID-like, and several supporting references, while removing Learning by Seeing More Classes and the Open-world Machine Learning review. It adds explicit positioning against externally sourced negative-label knowledge. The central distinction between global-prompt optimization and local-prompt enhancement remains intact.

P1.justification: V2 renames the paper and method, updates author and publication information, clarifies prompt/feature terminology, adjusts subsection organization, and slightly reorders results. Most existing prose and the main narrative remain recognizable; the new appendix largely documents added scientific material.

P2.justification: V2 adopts ICLR typography and layout, revises Figures 1–2, changes table styling, and converts v1 Table 7 into a bar-chart ablation. It also adds multiple comparison and sensitivity tables, hard-OOD illustrations, regional-number curves, expanded density plots, and heatmaps. These are substantial display changes beyond pagination.

improvement.justification: V2 supplies previously missing training and crop/regional-selection parameters needed for reproduction and directly tests sensitivity to important design choices. Together with the new comparisons and explicit limitations, this substantially strengthens the paper's assessability and empirical support. Localized reporting flaws remain: the revised Table 6 contradicts its retained discussion, and Table 14's interpretation mixes k columns. These flaws do not outweigh the substantial gains.
